subject: mathematics
question_text: If a = 2i+j−k, b = −i+2j−4k and c = i+j+k, then find (a×b)·(b×c).

verification.note: Source: Baby Bullet-Q, Junior Inter Maths-1A (Sri Publishers, Machilipatnam), book p.35 — LAQ chapter 4 Product of Vectors, answer 21.1, on a ★★★ SSP (Super Scoring Page). recall_prompt: Say how you would work out this product — say which pieces you compute first and how you finish.

steps.label: Write what is given
steps.margin_note: No mark of its own. Copy the three vectors out once, in i, j, k order. Both cross products below are read straight off these rows, so a slip here is repeated twice.
steps.memory_tip: Copy the three vectors out once in i, j, k order before any determinant.

recall.must_convey: That the given vectors are written out before any product is computed. Naming the step is full credit.
accept: write the given vectors out first
copy down a b and c before starting
note the given vectors in i j k form
ichina vectors ni modata rasta
start by writing what is given

steps.why: A cross product is a determinant whose rows ARE these vectors. Laying them out once, aligned, is what makes each determinant readable.
common_mistakes: Missing a zero component and shifting a whole row.
Copying a sign wrongly and carrying it through every product.

steps.label: Find a×b
steps.margin_note: Two of the eight marks. Write the determinant with i, j, k on top and the two vectors as the rows BELOW, in the order they appear in the product — a first, then b.
steps.memory_tip: i, j, k on top and the two vectors as rows BELOW, in the order the product names them.

recall.must_convey: That a×b is set out as a determinant with a on the first row and b on the second, and evaluates to −2i + 9j + 5k.
accept: write the determinant with i j k on top then a then b and expand to get minus two i plus nine j plus five k
cross a with b using the determinant, the answer is minus two i plus nine j plus five k
expand the cross product determinant for a cross b
a cross b determinant rasi expand cheste minus two i plus nine j plus five k vasthundi
take the cross product of a and b first

steps.why: The middle term carries a minus sign in front — that is part of the expansion, not part of the numbers, and it is where most sign errors enter.
common_mistakes: Writing b on the first row and a on the second, which reverses the answer.
Forgetting the minus in front of the j term.

steps.label: Find b×c
steps.margin_note: Two more marks. Same construction, but the rows are b then c. Note that b appears in BOTH products — copy the same row, do not recompute it differently.
steps.memory_tip: b appears in BOTH products — copy the same row rather than recomputing it differently.

recall.must_convey: That b×c is computed the same way, with b on the first row and c on the second, giving 6i − 3j − 3k.
accept: do the same for b cross c to get six i minus three j minus three k
cross b with c using the determinant
b cross c comes to six i minus three j minus three k
b cross c kuda ade vidhanga determinant tho
take the second cross product

steps.why: b sits in both products, so its row is written twice. Checking that the two copies match is a free way to catch a transcription slip.
common_mistakes: Computing c×b instead, which flips every sign.

steps.label: Take the dot product
steps.margin_note: Three marks. This is a DOT product of the two results — multiply matching components and add. The answer is a single number, not a vector.
steps.memory_tip: This is a DOT product of the two results: multiply matching components and add. The answer is a number.

recall.must_convey: That the two results are combined with a DOT product — matching components multiplied and added — not another cross product.
accept: dot the two results together, multiply matching components and add
take the scalar product of the two vectors found
this one is a dot product so the answer is a number
rendu results ni dot product cheyyali, number vasthundi
multiply component by component and add them

steps.why: The bracket in the question is a DOT between two cross products. Getting that outer operation right is what decides whether the answer is a number or a vector.
common_mistakes: Taking a cross product of the two results.
Adding the components instead of multiplying first.

steps.label: State the value
steps.margin_note: Last mark. Add the three terms. All three are negative here, so the total is negative — a positive answer means a sign was dropped.
steps.memory_tip: All three terms are negative here, so the total is negative. A positive answer means a dropped sign.

recall.must_convey: That the three products add to −54.
accept: minus twelve minus twenty seven minus fifteen is minus fifty four
the answer is minus fifty four
it comes to negative fifty four
minus fifty four vasthundi
the value is minus fifty four

steps.why: A scalar triple-style product like this is just a number, and the sign of that number carries meaning — so it must be reported, not dropped.
common_mistakes: Leaving the answer as three unadded terms.

insider_note: b appears in both brackets, but they are still two separate cross products. The last step is a DOT product, so the answer is the single number −54 and not a vector.
